title_en: Beijing Siweige-Taide Electronic Engineering Company v. Beijing Yinlan Technology Company and Liu Yongchun et al. — unfair competition dispute

full_text_en:
Beijing Sweiger-Taide Electronic Engineering Company v.

Beijing Yinlan Technology Company and Liu Yongchun et al.

— dispute over unfair competition

Plaintiff: Beijing Sweiger-Taide Electronic Engineering Co., Ltd.

Legal Representative: Tian Lin, General Manager

Defendant: Beijing Yinlan Technology Company

Legal Representative: Gao Shouzu, Manager

Defendant: Liu Yongchun, staff member of the Golden Card Department of Beijing Yinlan Technology Company

Defendant: Cong Weizi, staff member of the Golden Card Department of Beijing Yinlan Technology Company

Defendant: Liu Shenghong, staff member of the Golden Card Department of Beijing Yinlan Technology Company

Defendant: Lou Jingtao, unemployed

Defendant: Dang Hongzhe, unemployed

The plaintiff, Beijing Sweiger-Taide Electronic Engineering Company (hereinafter referred to as Taide Company), filed a lawsuit with the Haidian District People's Court of Beijing against the defendant, Beijing Yinlan Technology Company (hereinafter referred to as Yinlan Company), and the defendants Liu Yongchun, Cong Weizi, Liu Shenghong, Lou Jingtao, Dang Hongzhe, and others for unfair competition.

The plaintiff alleged: The defendants Liu Yongchun, Cong Weizi, Liu Shenghong, Lou Jingtao, and Dang Hongzhe, taking advantage of their access to the plaintiff's technical and business information, colluded with the defendant Yinlan Company to engage in unfair competition against the plaintiff, resulting in a significant decline in the plaintiff's product sales and causing substantial economic and goodwill losses. The plaintiff requested the court to: 1. Order the defendants to immediately cease the development and sale of the IC card management system and destroy the illegally copied software, hardware, and various materials; 2. Order the defendants to publicly apologize to the plaintiff and guarantee not to infringe upon the plaintiff's products in the future; 3. Order the defendants to compensate the plaintiff for economic losses and goodwill damage of RMB 300,000 and bear the attorney fees and litigation costs of this case.

The defendant Yinlan Company argued: Although the staff of its Golden Card Department had worked for the plaintiff for a period of time, they did not have access to the plaintiff's trade secrets or business secrets. The defendant, after notarization, copied the software of the plaintiff's IC card technology from the plaintiff's former clients. This fact demonstrates that the plaintiff did not take any confidentiality measures regarding its own technical secrets and did not require its clients to keep them confidential. This was the cause of the leakage of the plaintiff's technical secrets. Currently, IC card technology is already a publicly available applied technology, and the plaintiff does not hold exclusive rights to the IC card management system. During the development and sale of IC card technology, the defendant's Golden Card Department did not infringe upon the plaintiff's trade secrets. Because the plaintiff's after-sales service was not timely and the quality of its products and projects was low, its former clients came to the defendant for service. This is the defendant's business right and has nothing to do with the plaintiff. The defendant did not use the plaintiff's business secrets, and the court should dismiss the plaintiff's claims.

The defendants Liu Yongchun and Cong Weizi agreed with the defense of the defendant Yinlan Company.

The defendants Lou Jingtao and Dang Hongzhe argued: We are not employees of Yinlan Company, and the plaintiff's accusation of infringement against us is unfounded. The court should dismiss the plaintiff's claims against us.

The Haidian District People's Court of Beijing found the following facts upon trial:

The plaintiff, Taide Company, began investing funds in 1993 to research and develop an IC card management system. By 1995, it had completed the IC card software development and hardware design for systems such as cafeteria meal sales, shopping mall management, credential management, and attendance tracking, and had promoted and used them in universities and enterprises. Between June 1995 and November 1996, the defendants Liu Yongchun, Cong Weizi, Liu Shenghong, Dang Hongzhe, and Lou Jingtao each signed labor contracts and agreements with Taide Company (Party A). Article 7 of the labor contracts stipulated: "(2) If Party B fails to complete work tasks on time or leaks Party A's confidential information due to Party B's reasons, Party B must bear necessary economic losses and legal liability; (3) If Party B is engaged in the management, development, or research of patents, proprietary technology, or trade secrets during employment, Party B shall not engage in work related to patents, proprietary technology, or trade secrets within three years after the termination of the technical contract; otherwise, it shall be deemed an infringement." The agreement stipulated: All IC card application technologies (materials, software programs, hardware designs), including software and hardware technologies developed by Party B during employment, belong to Taide Company; Party B shall not appropriate such technologies or transfer them to others for product development; upon leaving, Party B shall return all materials, software programs, hardware designs, etc., to Taide Company; if Party B commits any breach, Taide Company has the right to pursue Party B's legal liability.

On March 24, 1997, defendant Liu Yongchun signed a contract with defendant Yinlan Company to establish the Golden Card Department of Yinlan Company, with employees including Liu Yongchun and defendants Cong Weizi and Liu Shenghong. From April to July of the same year, Liu Yongchun, Liu Shenghong, Cong Weizi, and defendants Lou Jingtao and Dang Hongzhe resigned from Taide Company. Cong Weizi had previously represented the plaintiff Taide Company in signing the "Guiyou Shopping Card (IC Card) Project" contract with Beijing Guiyou Mansion Co., Ltd., and Taide Company had fully performed all obligations under that contract. In March 1997, Wu Weidong, an employee of Guiyou Mansion Co., Ltd., called Taide Company to inquire about purchasing IC cards. Cong Weizi answered the call and notified Liu Yongchun to contact Wu Weidong. After negotiating and agreeing on matters including fees, when it came time to sign the contract, Cong Weizi only then stated that he was an employee of Yinlan Company and requested that Guiyou Mansion Co., Ltd. sign the contract with Yinlan Company. On March 26, 1997, Cong Weizi, representing Yinlan Company, signed a contract with Luo Min, an employee of Beijing Guiyou Mansion Co., Ltd., for the purchase of IC cards, with a contract amount of RMB 165,000. On May 16, 1997, Cong Weizi again signed a contract with Luo Min for the purchase of 10 YPR-type IC card readers/writers at a unit price of RMB 2,250, totaling RMB 22,500. Wu Weidong of Beijing Guiyou Mansion Co., Ltd. confirmed that the 10 YPR-type IC card readers/writers purchased by Guiyou Mansion Co., Ltd. from Yinlan Company differed from Taide Company's readers/writers only by the replacement of a chip, with added security features on the original basis. On June 18, 1997, Yinlan Company sold one IC card socket to Beijing University of Science and Technology for RMB 3,600. Kang Jian, a cadre at Beijing University of Science and Technology, confirmed that Liu Yongchun had repeatedly copied Taide Company's IC card software from the university. In July 1997, Cong Weizi, representing Yinlan Company, signed a contract with Changchun Beixi Development Co., Ltd., selling nine YPR card issuing management machines (unit price RMB 2,150), software valued at RMB 10,000, gold and silver membership cards totaling RMB 27,000, with a project cost of RMB 56,350. On June 23, 1997, Cong Weizi, representing Yinlan Company, signed a contract with Beijing Jinyue Development Company (i.e., the Beijing Commodity Inspection Bureau project) for a contract amount of RMB 21,700, including five YD charging machines (unit price RMB 2,850), one YDR card issuing management machine (unit price RMB 2,450), and software fees of RMB 5,000. On July 10, 1997, Yinlan Company signed a contract with Beijing Health School for a contract amount of RMB 116,813, including 15 YD charging machines (unit price RMB 2,450), one YDR card issuing management machine (unit price RMB 2,150), and one set of software valued at RMB 10,000. The IC cards were subsequently seized by the court, and the project had not yet been completed. In August 1997, after filing the lawsuit, Taide Company applied for evidence preservation. An inspection of the two seized computers of Yinlan Company revealed that the first computer's C drive LSH directory contained copies of 14 IC card management system software programs of Taide Company, all marked with Taide Company's logo; the programs copied on the second computer partially bore Taide Company's markings, and partially were modifications of Taide Company's software. Among the preserved evidence were also two copies of Taide Company's TL-901S schematic diagrams, two copies of TL-901S shell design drawings, one copy of TL-901K schematic diagram, three copies of TL-901S upper computer source program materials, four copies of TL-901S lower computer source programs, one copy of TL-901HE lower computer source program, one copy of TL-901K lower computer source program, Taide Company's client list materials, Taide Company's promotional and technical materials, and a compilation of materials. It was also found that in a note dated March 27, 1997, Liu Shenghong recorded: Modifications to Taide Company's reader/writer program: (1) Original card siemers4432, (2) New card simers4432, the new program can use both types of cards (05/15) The upper computer program only needs to modify the configidbf file, changing the card type to B62307 (development card password remains 160208). A note dated May 8, 1997, recorded: "Guiyou program: Since the new board is not quite the same as the old board, the eprom has been changed from one chip to four chips, and the chip select signal has changed, resulting in an emor-0 error (read/write eprom error). As explained on the left, simply jumper the circuit board to solve the problem."

The Haidian District People's Court of Beijing held:

The focus of this dispute is whether the plaintiff Taide Company's "IC Card Series Management System" constitutes a trade secret. Pursuant to Article 10, Paragraph 3 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China, a trade secret must meet four requirements: 1. It is not known to the public, i.e., it has the secrecy of being unknown to unspecified persons; 2. It can bring economic benefits to the rights holder, i.e., it has certain economic value; 3. It has practicality, i.e., the trade secret must have actual use value and not merely remain at a theoretical level; 4. The rights holder must take confidentiality measures; if the rights holder does not take such measures, it indicates that the rights holder itself is not aware that its technical information and business information constitute trade secrets, and the law cannot protect them. The IC card technology developed by Taide Company with substantial investment of human and financial resources received positive feedback from users upon being marketed, bringing good economic benefits to the company. Taide Company did not register the copyright of the computer software for this technology but protected it by signing confidentiality agreements with employees and strengthening internal management, thereby keeping its technology and business information in a state of secrecy unknown to the public. Therefore, Taide Company's IC card technical information and business information constitute trade secrets and should be protected by law. Although IC card technology systems may be functionally similar, from a technical perspective, the software supporting the systems has significant differences in source programs, schematic diagrams, and other aspects; even if the results are similar, the approaches and means to achieve them are vastly different. The defendant Yinlan Company's argument that Taide Company's IC card technology is publicly known technology and could also be obtained through "reverse engineering," and thus does not constitute a trade secret, cannot be sustained. IC card technology is a system engineering technology. Taide Company not only provides products to clients but is also responsible for installation, commissioning, and maintenance during use. Clients merely use and manage the IC card system provided by Taide Company and do not have access to the substance of the technology. Therefore, the trade secrets of the IC card technology have always remained in the hands of Taide Company, and it was not necessary for the company to sign confidentiality agreements with clients. Yinlan Company's argument that Taide Company's IC card technology does not constitute a trade secret because it did not sign confidentiality agreements with clients is also unfounded and is not accepted.

Article 10, Paragraph 1, Item (3) of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law stipulates: "Disclosing, using, or allowing others to use the trade secrets in their possession in violation of an agreement or the rights holder's confidentiality requirements" constitutes an act of unfair competition by infringing upon trade secrets. Modern trade secret rights holders, for the needs of their work, must allow their employees to possess and use trade secrets. To prevent the disclosure of trade secrets, the law permits rights holders to restrict employees by signing confidentiality agreements to prevent them from leaking the company's trade secrets. Employees, whether during their employment or after leaving, must keep secrets as agreed. The labor contracts and confidentiality agreements signed between the plaintiff Taide Company and the defendants Liu Yongchun, Liu Shenghong, Cong Weizi, Lou Jingtao, and Dang Hongzhe represent the true intentions of both parties, are lawful and valid, and both parties must strictly comply. Liu Yongchun, Cong Weizi, and Liu Shenghong violated the contract agreements. While still working for Taide Company, they secretly worked part-time for the defendant Yinlan Company, established the Golden Card Department of Yinlan Company, used the business secrets of Taide Company, and improperly appropriated the "Guiyou Mansion IC Card Project" business that originally belonged to Taide Company. They also used the technical secrets of Taide Company to slightly modify Taide Company's TL-901SS reader/writer, renamed it the YPR-type IC card reader/writer, slightly modified Taide Company's software, and sold the IC card system under the name of Yinlan Company, even directly using product casings bearing the Taide Company logo. When Yinlan Company signed contracts with Changchun Beixi Development Co., Ltd., Beijing Jinyue Development Company, and Beijing Health School, Cong Weizi was still employed by Taide Company. Yinlan Company failed to provide evidence within the period specified by the court to prove that the technology used in the IC card management system projects of the aforementioned units was self-developed and researched, and it also refused to allow a comparative appraisal of its IC card management system software and hardware with Taide Company's products. After evidence preservation, it was discovered that Yinlan Company's computers stored a large number of Taide Company's IC card management system software programs; among the sealed and seized items of Yinlan Company were Taide Company's product design drawings, schematic diagrams, client lists, software programs, modified IC card management system materials, and physical objects. These facts prove that Yinlan Company and Liu Yongchun, Cong Weizi, and Liu Shenghong were using Taide Company's trade secrets to engage in unfair competition against Taide Company and seek illegal profits, constituting an infringement of Taide Company's trade secrets and should bear corresponding tort liability. Taide Company's request for the above defendants to cease the infringement and publicly apologize has justified grounds and should be supported; its economic losses, calculated in accordance with Article 20, Paragraph 1 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, based on the profits gained by the defendants during the infringement period, amount to RMB 136,450. The portion of the claim exceeding this amount is not recognized. The defendants Dang Hongzhe and Lou Jingtao, although having worked for Taide Company, did not go to Yinlan Company's Golden Card Department after resigning. Taide Company's request for Dang Hongzhe and Lou Jingtao to bear tort liability lacks factual basis and is not supported.

In summary, the Haidian District People's Court of Beijing rendered the following judgment on December 1, 1997:

1. The defendants Beijing Yinlan Technology Company, Liu Yongchun, Cong Weizi, and Liu Shenghong shall publish an apology to the plaintiff Beijing Sweiger-Taide Electronic Engineering Co., Ltd. in a nationally distributed non-professional newspaper or periodical;

2. The defendants Beijing Yinlan Technology Company, Liu Yongchun, Cong Weizi, and Liu Shenghong shall cease disclosing and using the trade secrets of the plaintiff Beijing Sweiger-Taide Electronic Engineering Co., Ltd.'s IC card management system;

3. The defendants Beijing Yinlan Technology Company, Liu Yongchun, Cong Weizi, and Liu Shenghong shall compensate the plaintiff Beijing Sweiger-Taide Electronic Engineering Co., Ltd. for economic losses of RMB 136,450 and for reasonable litigation expenses of RMB 20,000;

4. The plaintiff Beijing Sweiger-Taide Electronic Engineering Co., Ltd.'s claim for tort liability against the defendants Lou Jingtao and Dang Hongzhe is dismissed.

The case acceptance fee of RMB 10,010 and the litigation preservation fee of RMB 3,020 shall be borne by the defendants Beijing Yinlan Technology Company, Liu Yongchun, Cong Weizi, and Liu Shenghong.

After the judgment was pronounced, neither party appealed.
